blindSummary: Religion-based identity verification doubles as an outing mechanism for gender-nonconforming visitors at public festivals. After a right-wing religious organisation publicly urged organisers of a major autumn dance festival not to allow members of other religions and to check government identity cards for entry, a political row erupted; in a city of this state/province organisers imposed identity-card verification, security checks with "male and female" boundaries and a ritual bow before a deity statue as entry conditions. An identity-checked, religion-screened entry gate at a public festival is precisely the mechanism by which a gender-nonconforming visitor is examined and outed by authorities who are not supposed to be involved — and it is happening in named cities, not nationwide. National backdrop from this record's sources: parliament passed a 2026 amendment bill removing the right to self-identify, limiting recognition to historically accepted socio-cultural groups and intersex people, mandating medical certification for gender-affirming procedures, and creating offences of "coercing or alluring" a person to be transgender punishable with up to life in prison — prompting nationwide protests from trans communities, with the top court's appointed panel asking the government to withdraw it; the national census recorded 487,803 transgender persons but only about 32,500 hold the identity cards needed for social security.
blindSourceSummaries: International human rights organisation news analysis (26 Mar 2026): parliament passed a 2026 amendment bill to the national transgender-persons protection act — removes the right to self-identification, limits legal recognition to traditionally accepted socio-cultural communities (locally named third-gender groups) and intersex people, mandates medical certification, and introduces offences of "coercing or alluring" with up to life imprisonment; effectively reverses the country's 2014 top-court self-determination ruling; protest held in the capital 25 March 2026; last census recorded 487,803 trans persons, only ~32,500 identity cards issued.

Public broadcaster news report (26 Mar 2026): the amendment bill cleared both houses of parliament and awaits presidential assent; narrows recognition to biological/physical traits, intersex variations and traditional community identities; mandatory medical-board and district-authority certification for gender-affirming surgery; ~2 million trans people estimated in the country; multiple rallies against the bill; top court-appointed advisory panel urged withdrawal; opposition and trans activists call it an attack on privacy, dignity and the 2014 ruling.

National daily news report (18 Aug 2024): a group of trans women travelling to a protest in another state were subjected to a "gender check" at a metro station, where an in-service railway protection constable allegedly groped one of them to check her gender and made a lewd remark; she filed a police complaint; metro and railway protection forces denied the allegations and counter-filed a case against the group; a case was registered under the national transgender-persons protection act. Note: the incident occurred in another state — documents centralised transit-policing behaviour toward trans travellers nationwide, not this region specifically.
blindTangential: The 2026 national amendment bill strips self-identification, adds anti-"coercion" offences and mandates medical certification — a national climate that raises the cost of being recognised as trans in public in this region as elsewhere, even though it is not region-specific; festival-gate identity screening (this region's own finding) becomes a more acute outing risk under a regime that narrows legal recognition.
